description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.desc: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is practicing for the Baltimore Ravens Friday according to Jamison Hensley.
items.impact: Jackson has been able to log limited practice session over the past couple of days as the quarterback continues to work back from a two-game absence for head coach Jesse Minter. Fantasy managers will need to monitor the team's injury report ahead of a potential return against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7.
items.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practicing Friday

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.desc: Sam Franklin Jr. had his suspension reduced to a $14,926 fine according to Adam Schefter.
items.impact: Franklin Jr. was part of multiple Buffalo defenders that engaged in unsportsmanlike conduct against the Las Vegas Raiders, ultimately resulting in the fine after a league hearing.
items.title: Sam Franklin Jr. has suspension reduced

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Drake Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, adding 26 yards and another touchdown on four carries during Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: The Patriots certainly wanted the win, but fantasy managers enjoyed a big performance from Maye. The third-year QB threw for more than 300 yards for the second time in the last three weeks, and he's now scored 11 total touchdowns during that span. Maye will be a certain start at Miami in Week 8.
items.title: Drake Maye accounts for three touchdowns in Week 7 loss

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson gained just nine yards on three carries and caught two passes for 14 yards in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Henderson has now averaged just six touches per game over the last three weeks, and he's done very little with them. As surprising as it seems, Henderson's fantasy value is basically relegated to being a handcuff for veteran Rhamondre Stevenson at the moment.
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson gets just five touches in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Rhamondre Stevenson gained just 22 yards on six carries, but hauled in all five of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Stevenson's six carries were a team high Thursday night, but the Patriots just did not do much on the ground. More importantly for fantasy managers, Stevenson also led the team in receiving yards. The veteran running back scored on a 48-yard passing play, and he was far more involved than TreVeyon Henderson. Stevenson will remain in the RB2 or Flex range for Week 8.
items.title: Rhamondre Stevenson delivers in passing game Thursday night

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Cole Kmet (knee) is believed to have suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Bears Thursday night win over the Patriots. He will undergo an MRI today to determine the full severity.
items.impact: Kmet had some nice involvement in this game before going down due to injury, and it's now especially unfortunate that he is expected to have this absence extend for the rest of the season. Colston Loveland will see more work for sure, but don't count out Sam Roush, who should also see more snaps.
items.title: Cole Kmet (knee) believed to have season-ending knee injury

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: A.J. Brown hauled in 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Since returning from a four-week absence, Brown has now secured just 6-of-16 targets for 75 yards over the last two games. He looked a little more up to speed Thursday night, but he's still well below the top-tier fantasy option he once was. Better games should be on the way from Brown, but right now, he's difficult to trust in fantasy lineups.
items.title: A.J. Brown grabs three passes in Thursday's loss

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: DeMario Douglas brought in 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Douglas delivered back-to-back big games in Week and Week 6, but he fell back down to Earth against the Bears. Drake Maye heavily relied on his running backs and tight ends Thursday night, not leaving much for Douglas behind fellow wideout A.J. Brown. Douglas may have already had his best games of the season and will likely be tough to rely on for fantasy purposes going forward this season.
items.title: DeMario Douglas catches three passes in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Eli Raridon secured 3-of-4 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Raridon emerged during a five-catch performance back in Week 5. He almost disappeared in Week 6, but the rookie third-rounder stepped back up Thursday night. Raridon scored his second career TD on a 30-yard strike from QB Drake Maye in the third quarter of this one, and he's certainly a talented young player for fantasy managers to keep tabs on.
items.title: Eli Raridon hits paydirt in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Hunter Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Henry led all Patriots pass catchers in targets and receptions Thursday night. The veteran remains a reliable option for QB Drake Maye, as he's caught at least three passes and gone over 40 yards in each of the past four weeks. Henry has also scored twice in that span.
items.title: Hunter Henry leads Patriots in receptions Thursday night

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Andy Borregales made his only field-goal attempts and 3-of-3 PATs in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: Borregales is now 9-of-11 on field-goal tries and 17-of-18 on PATs through seven games. The second-year kicker has been solid this season, but he has yet to crack double figures in any week.
items.title: Andy Borregales puts six points on board in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: The Patriots' defense gave up 30 points and more than 400 yards of total offense in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears.
items.impact: The Patriots did come up with three sacks on Bears QB Caleb Williams, but that was about the extent of the positives in Thursday's loss. The Patriots defense was coming off a couple of solid showings against the Raiders and Jets, but the Bears' high-powered offense in Chicago proved to be too much to handle for most of the night. Still, the Dolphins await in Week 8, which will make the Patriots unit a popular choice for fantasy managers.
items.title: Patriots D/ST records three sacks, gives up 30 points in Week 7 loss

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Caleb Douglas (ankle) is expected to play against the Jets on Sunday.
items.impact: After a strong NFL debut back in Week 1, Douglas was knocked out early in his second career game and has not played for the Dolphins since. That should change this week, as the rookie has been active at practice leading into a divisional matchup against the Jets. Fellow rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. likely stands to lose snaps if Douglas does return.
items.title: Caleb Douglas (ankle) expected to play in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Breece Hall (quad) has been listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
items.impact: Hall returned to practice in a limited capacity on Thursday, and it appears he has at least a chance to finally return to the Jets' backfield this week. The dual-threat back has not played since Week 3, ceding a workhorse role to backup Braelon Allen, who has been quite productive with the opportunity. If Hall does return, he could be on a limited snap count, sharing the load with Allen.
items.title: Breece Hall (quad) questionable for Sunday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play Sunday against the Dolphins.
items.impact: Mitchell has not played since Week 2, but he has been practicing this week and will return to the field Sunday. Mitchell was off to a strong start for the Jets this season, hauling in 9-of-15 targets for 123 yards over the first two games. With Garrett Wilson and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. both out there as well, it will be interesting to see how Mitchell works back into the mix.
items.title: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will return in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: The Bears defense allowed 24 points on 380 yards of total offense, recording two sacks and one interception in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: The Bears did not exactly shut down the Patriots' offense on Thursday night, especially through the air, allowing Drake Maye to throw for better than 300 yards and two touchdowns. The Chicago unit did contain an almost non-existent Patriots' running game. The Bears defense did come up with a few impact plays, and should be a middle-tier fantasy option. The Seahawks await in Week 8.
items.title: Bears D/ST comes up with two sacks, one interception in Week 7 win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Cairo Santos made 3-of-4 field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Santos made the longest field goal of his 13-year career Thursday night, connecting on a 58-yard attempt to put the Bears up by nine points with about 90 seconds remaining in regulation. Santos has hit 11 of 15 FG attempts overall this season. He has also been perfect on 21 PATs.
items.title: Cairo Santos puts a dozen points on the board Thursday night

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Colston Loveland hauled in 7-of-12 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Those who have been patient with Loveland after a frustratingly slow start to the season are now being rewarded. With Caleb Williams back in the huddle for the last two games, Loveland has looked like the No. 1 option in the Bears' passing attack. The second-year TE has caught 13 of 19 targets for 134 yards and a pair of touchdowns in that span. Loveland should remain a strong TE1 the rest of the way.
items.title: Colston Loveland finds the end zone again in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Kalif Raymond did not catch either of his two targets in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Even with Caleb Williams back under center, Raymond has seen just two targets in each of the last two games. The veteran receiver got off to a strong start over the first three weeks of the season and looked like he was going to be a significant contributor for the Bears' offense. That has not remained the case, however, and Raymond can be cut loose in most fantasy leagues.
items.title: Kalif Raymond puts up a goose egg in Week 7

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Rome Odunze secured 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Odunze seems to still be third in the pecking order of Bears pass catchers behind TE Colston Loveland and fellow wideout Luther Burden. Still, Odunze turned in a solid effort Thursday night. Over the last two games with QB Caleb Williams back at the helm of the offense, Odunze has come up with 7-of-9 targets for 108 yards. The third-year pro has 24 receptions with an average of 15.9 yards per catch through seven games.
items.title: Rome Odunze hauls in four passes Thursday night

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Luther Burden III caught all four of his targets for 130 yards and a touchdown, adding a seven-yard run in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Burden and QB Caleb Williams have certainly been on the same page since the latter returned from injury in Week 6. Over the last two games, Burden has come up with all 12 of his targets for a combined 225 yards. The second-year receiver gained a season-high 130 yards on Thursday night, recording the third 100-yard effort of his career. Burden is solidifying himself in the WR2 range for standard fantasy leagues.
items.title: Luther Burden III shows off big-play skills Thursday night

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Roschon Johnson gained 13 yards on two carries in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: After totaling 85 yards and a touchdown on 15 touches in Week 6, Johnson almost disappeared from the box score in Week 7. Even with Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) still sidelined, Johnson wasn't given much of an opportunity behind starting RB D'Andre Swift, who had 26 touches on the night.
items.title: Roschon Johnson does little in Week 7 win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: D'Andre Swift rushed for 78 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, adding four receptions for 12 yards in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: With Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) still out and Roschon Johnson not very involved, Swift shouldered a workhorse load against the Patriots on Thursday night. The dual-threat back averaged less than 3.5 yards per touch, but he did find the end zone for the seventh time this season, which has him currently tied for second in the NFL in rushing touchdowns. Swift will go up against the Seahawks' defense in Week 8. He remains a low-end RB1 for standard fantasy leagues.
items.title: D'Andre Swift finds the end zone in Week 7 win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Caleb Williams completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
items.impact: Williams added 18 yards on five carries to his strong stat line from Thursday night. The third-year pro has been excellent since returning from injury, leading the Bears to two victories over the past five days. Williams has cleared 300 yards in each of those games, tossing three touchdowns without an interception.
items.title: Caleb Williams throws for more than 300 yards in Week 7 win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Anton Harrison will miss the rest of the season due to a torn ACL.
items.impact: Harrison was placed on IR last week and underwent what was expected to be an arthroscopic procedure on Thursday. Unfortunately, it was revealed that Harrison had suffered a tear of his ACL, which is a much more serious issue with a longer-term recovery process. Walker Little should continue to start in Harrison's place.
items.title: Anton Harrison (knee) to miss rest of season
